entities.summary: Pope Sabinian was the bishop of Rome from 13 September 604 to his death on 22 February 606, marking the beginning of the papacy's Eastern Roman domination. His pontificate was characterized by a series of diplomatic exchanges with the Byzantine Empire, as he sought to maintain the Church's influence in the face of growing imperial power. The Fourth Council of Constantinople, convened during Sabinian's papacy, further entrenched the Church's position within the empire. Sabinian's legacy is marked by his efforts to balance the Church's authority with the realities of imperial rule, setting a precedent for future popes to navigate the complex web of power between the Church and state. Through his tenure, the papacy emerged as a central institution in the Eastern Roman Empire, its influence extending to the farthest reaches of the Byzantine world.
